title: drosera indica var. dietrichiana
intro: Drosera indica var. dietrichiana, commonly known as Indian sundew, is a carnivorous plant species native to the Indian subcontinent. It is traditionally used in Ayurvedic medicine for its potential health benefits, including the treatment of various respiratory issues, fever, and digestive problems. The plant is believed to exhibit therapeutic actions such as anti-inflammatory, antimicrobial, and antitussive properties, which contribute to its use in traditional medicine. Bioactive constituents present in Indian sundew include iridoids, flavonoids, and phenolic acids, which are thought to be responsible for its medicinal properties.
